title: The arrangement of the first eight cells is not a constant character of a species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The arrangement of the first eight cells is not a constant character of a species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A particular arrangement of cell partitions at the eight-celled stage is not a specific or constant character of an organism; within a single species such as the frog, several essentially different arrangements occur.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: is a particular arrangement of cell-partitions to be looked upon (as the published figures of the embryologist are apt to suggest) as a _specific character_, or at least a constant or normal character, of the particular organism? The answer to this question is a direct negative

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Eight-cell arrangements as specific characters”. Scope: eight-celled stage of eggs, especially the animal pole of the frog’s egg

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A single well-imaged species with multiple distinct arrangements refutes constancy, making the criterion simple and decisive. Open embryo datasets with replicates support this analysis now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify eight-cell partition topology in multiple embryos from the same species and test whether more than one essentially different arrangement occurs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Equivalent 3D arrangements can look different in 2D projections.

Some datasets contain few embryos per species.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.94
analysis feasibility: 0.84
operationalizability: 0.98
data existence: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Within-species variability of the eight-cell pattern is a direct frequency question, and frog cleavage images are public. They are not a random sample of eggs with arrangements already scored, so a small team would still be compiling rather than downloading a finished census. The test is well posed and only partly executable on what is archived.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify the surface partition pattern of many eight-cell frog eggs and test whether more than one topological type occurs at appreciable frequency. Several recurring arrangements within the species would support the claim; a single arrangement in nearly every egg would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A frequency count needs many individual eggs, and public atlases are not already tabulated that way.

Atlas images preferentially show a textbook arrangement, which is the sampling bias the claim is warning against.
